main_result.title: Process-level rare-mismatch inference can remain anytime-valid under arbitrary cross-cluster mean drift by targeting the average conditional mean directly; a fixed bounded-mgf mixture keeps O(1/m) zero-mismatch resolution rather than paying a generic Hoeffding O(1/m^2) price.

artifact.cluster_contract: one predeclared bounded Y_t in [0,1] per top-level process/workload/server-lifetime cluster; lower-level dependence may be arbitrary
artifact.default_weights: uniform over the eight fixed lambda components

derivation.convexity: For lambda>0 and y in [0,1], exp(-lambda*y) <= 1-(1-exp(-lambda))*y.
derivation.component_supermartingale: With a=1-exp(-lambda) and mu_i=E[Y_i|F_{i-1}], product_i exp(-lambda Y_i)/(1-a mu_i) is a nonnegative supermartingale.
derivation.average_reduction: log(1-a x) is concave, so product_i(1-a mu_i) <= (1-a mu_bar_t)^t. Therefore exp(-lambda sum Y_i)/(1-a mu_bar_t)^t is pathwise upper-bounded by that supermartingale.
derivation.mixture: A fixed convex mixture over lambda components remains upper-bounded by a nonnegative supermartingale. Ville therefore gives P(exists t: E_t(mu_bar_t)>=1/alpha)<=alpha.
derivation.confidence_endpoint: The mixture is nondecreasing in candidate m, so binary-search inversion gives an anytime-valid upper endpoint for the time-varying average conditional mean itself, without assuming a constant p.

why_this_matters: A generic sub-Gaussian/Hoeffding mixture for drifting means would need roughly O(1/m^2) zero-mismatch clusters to certify a rare rate m. The bounded chord construction exploits Y in [0,1] and remains O(1/m) on the zero path.

This removes the need to choose between 'stable-p lease or no useful rare-rate certificate'. Time-varying conditional mismatch burden can be tracked directly as an average, provided the top-level cluster sequence itself is prospectively defined.

It also sharpens the earlier warning from average-mean testing literature: adaptive predictable bets that are valid for a per-time conditional-mean null need not remain valid for an average-conditional-mean null, but a fixed mixture can be designed to remain valid.

comparison_to_stable_p_default_artifact.zero_path: At alpha=.05, stable-p nested betting needed 378 zero clusters for U<=1%, while the new drifting-average default mixture needs 368. This tiny difference is due to different fixed mixture grids, not a theorem that the drifting estimand is always easier.
comparison_to_stable_p_default_artifact.scope: The stable-p values and drifting-average values use different default mixtures and different estimands. They are operational comparisons, not a dominance proof.

implementation_sanity_not_proof.simulation: 30,000 Bernoulli trajectories per pattern, 500 clusters, alpha=.05, evaluated crossing at the true running average conditional mean.
implementation_sanity_not_proof.interpretation: All were below 5% in this implementation stress. Validity rests on the supermartingale domination derivation, not these simulations.

external_alignment.Chugg_Ramdas_2025: arXiv:2512.21300 explicitly targets average conditional means of bounded variables with no stationarity assumption and derives variance-adaptive CSs.
external_alignment.average_mean_eprocess_warning: A separate average-mean testing supplement distinguishes the stronger per-time conditional-mean null from the weaker running-average null and notes that fixed mixture strategies can be valid under both while arbitrary predictable betting strategies need not be.

measurement_validity_rules: If the operational quantity is average reliability across changing process lifetimes, estimate the average conditional mean directly rather than forcing a constant fingerprint rate.
Do not reuse an adaptive betting strategy merely because it was valid under a per-cluster stable-mean null; average-mean validity is a separate theorem/contract.
Fixed mixture components may be chosen from public or disjoint calibration before the current outcome, but selecting the lambda mixture after seeing the current cluster score is not free.
The top-level process/workload cluster remains the statistical unit; a drift-robust average-mean CS does not license request-level pseudoreplication.
scope_guards: The new CS targets the equal-cluster average conditional mean, not a request-weighted average when cluster sizes differ.
It does not turn retrospectively selected process cells into a prospective sequence.
Default lambda weights were not optimized against the current public mismatch outcomes.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Compare the new fixed bounded-mixture average CS against the 2025 Chugg-Ramdas variance-adaptive average-conditional-mean CS on rare zero/sparse mismatch streams, emphasizing finite-sample 0.1%-5% upper endpoints rather than generic width.

Build a process/server-lifetime fingerprint lease state machine that chooses stable-p versus drifting-average inference based only on pre-outcome configuration/stability evidence and never resets lifetime error budget on reclassification.
Optimize a predeclared lambda mixture for rare mismatch tolerances under a robust prior over zero/sparse cluster failures and check worst-case delay under occasional mismatches.
Continue public search for full repeated-output traces or explicit frozen scorer labels to resolve token-to-score/sign propagation.

exact_next_action: Benchmark the new drifting-average CS against the Chugg-Ramdas 2025 empirical-Bernstein average-mean CS in the low-rate regime, then decide whether the more complex variance-adaptive method materially improves process-level rare-mismatch certification.
